what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to require a bond for the full project value on the private 42 Highland Street sewer extension, naming the town as obligee.
The commission asked Wright-Pierce to review the town's wastewater plan for 236 Crossroad and report whether the lot can be served by the extension.
Wright-Pierce gave a design update on the Whum/Pratt Street extension, and the project is funded by a state revolving fund loan with the application due October 15th.

The commission held its position on the Whum apartments sewer fees, and Dan Hill will recheck the fee effective dates.

why_it_matters: The bond requirement decides who carries the cost if a privately built sewer extension is left unfinished, which bears on whether the risk falls on the developer or on sewer users and taxpayers.
Whether 236 Crossroad and other lots can join the extension, and what the Whum apartments pay in sewer fees, affect who connects to town sewer and how the cost is shared among ratepayers.

October 15th: the state revolving fund loan application for the sewer extension is due.

meetings.summary: The commission heard Mr. Toll's request to charge the earlier connection rates for the Lancaster Ave extension and voted to deny it, leaving current fees in place. It also heard an engineer on a Northfield Road lot and the sewer service area line, a peer review of the Highfield Village sewer extension, and approved the FY15 budget. Updates covered the leaking Lancaster Ave manhole and replacement of SCADA components.

minutes.headline: Sewer Commission denied Mr. Toll's request for pre-July connection fees on the Lancaster Ave extension
minutes.summary: The commission heard Mr. Toll's request to charge the earlier connection rates for the Lancaster Ave extension and voted to deny it, leaving current fees in place. It also heard an engineer on a Northfield Road lot and the sewer service area line, a peer review of the Highfield Village sewer extension, and approved the FY15 budget. Updates covered the leaking Lancaster Ave manhole and replacement of SCADA components.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the contractor was being told to repair the leaking manhole and whether a repair plan exists.

votes.motion: Deny Mr. Toll's request and leave the connection fees where they are.

budget_items.what_was_said: Connection charges rose in the fiscal 2014 budget process, and inflow and infiltration fees were added on a flow-down from the state and Leominster.
Mr. Toll said the combined connection and I&I increase was significant.
The one-time capacity payment is shown as revenue, with all but the first year placed in a reserve fund for the Fitchburg capacity payment.
Component quotes and programming cost were discussed. Buying the parts directly was favoured because the town is tax exempt.

budget_items.topic: Grease trap annual fee for new business
budget_items.what_was_said: A new restaurant would pay the annual fee for a full year without proration.

decisions.decision: Northfield Road lot matter continued to the next meeting; staff to check whether the service area line was a mapping error.
Highfield Village sewer plan vote deferred to the 11th, when the final plan with peer reviewer's approval is expected.
No vote on SCADA; the commission agreed to buy components directly and have the pump contractor install them, with details to be confirmed.
Next meeting set for February 11th.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to deny Mr. Toll's request to charge the earlier connection fees on the Lancaster Ave extension, leaving current fees in place.
The commission approved the fiscal year 15 budget.
A vote on the Highfield Village sewer extension plan was deferred to the 11th, when the final plan with the peer reviewer's approval is expected.
The Northfield Road lot matter was continued, and staff will check whether the sewer service area line was a mapping error.
No vote was taken on SCADA; the commission agreed to buy components directly and have the pump contractor install them.

why_it_matters: Sewer connection charges rose in the fiscal 2014 budget process, and the denial means anyone connecting to the Lancaster Ave extension pays the current fees, including the inflow and infiltration charge.
The Highfield Village payment is booked as revenue, with most of it held in a reserve for the Fitchburg capacity payment, so the extension's approval bears on future sewer costs for ratepayers.
watch_next: Next meeting February 11th: the Highfield Village sewer plan vote, with the final plan and peer reviewer's approval.
The Northfield Road lot matter returns at the next meeting, after staff check the service area line.
